title: Draft Electoral Rolls Released in Cuddalore, Villupuram and Kallakurichi for Checking
excerpt: Tamil Nadu's integrated draft electoral roll is out, with district lists published for Cuddalore, Villupuram and Kallakurichi. Voters have until December 11, 2026 to verify their details and seek additions, deletions or corrections before the final roll on January 4, 2027.
body:
• Integrated draft electoral rolls have been released for Cuddalore, Villupuram and Kallakurichi as district collectors published their district-level lists in Tamil Nadu.
  • Voters should check that their name appears and that their personal particulars, including name and address, are accurate.
  • Claims and objections for inclusion, deletion or correction can be submitted until December 11, 2026.
  • Decisions are scheduled by December 28, 2026, and the final electoral roll is due on January 4, 2027.

The integrated draft electoral roll has been released in Cuddalore, Villupuram and Kallakurichi, opening a public checking period for voters in the three Tamil Nadu districts. The release forms part of the state's draft publication, under which Chief Electoral Officer Archana Patnaik released the integrated draft electoral roll and district collectors published the respective district-level lists, according to BizzBuzz.

The publication follows two months of work under the Special Summary Revision. Over that period, electoral authorities worked on the inclusion of eligible voters, the deletion of names and the updating of entries in the electoral roll. The draft reflects the work completed during that period and is now available for public scrutiny.

What voters in the three districts should check

The immediate step for a voter in Cuddalore, Villupuram or Kallakurichi is to check whether their name appears on the list. Voters should also verify the accuracy of the personal particulars recorded against their name, because the claims period is the stage at which omissions and errors can be brought to the attention of electoral authorities before the roll is finalised.

Residents who find an error can seek a correction to particulars such as their name or address. A person whose name is missing can seek inclusion, and entries that require deletion can also be raised during the same window. Eligible new voters who have not yet enrolled will have an opportunity to apply during this period.

Mirror Now reported that people who are not currently listed, or who turn 18 by the qualifying dates of January 1, April 1, July 1 or October 1, can apply for inclusion using Form 6. The same report said applications for inclusion, deletion, modification or transposition of entries can be filed online through the official Election Commission voter portal or the ECINET mobile application.

The wider Tamil Nadu picture

Across Tamil Nadu, the draft rolls record a total electorate of 5.77 crore, a net increase of 403,327 voters since the previous rolls were published on April 6, Mirror Now reported. The breakdown provided by Chief Electoral Officer Archana Patnaik put the state's voter base at 2,82,03,992 men, 2,95,34,734 women and 7,892 third-gender voters.

Those statewide figures are the context for the district lists now open for checking in Cuddalore, Villupuram and Kallakurichi. The draft stage does not by itself settle an entry: applications and objections received during the checking period are examined before the final roll is prepared.

Dates to keep in mind

Applications and objections concerning inclusion, deletion and correction of entries can be submitted until December 11, 2026. Applications received during the window will be examined, with decisions scheduled by December 28, 2026.

The final electoral roll will then be published on January 4, 2027, incorporating the changes accepted during the scrutiny of claims and objections. For voters, that timetable makes the period before December 11 the time to act: check that a name is present, check that the details recorded are correct, and submit any request for inclusion or correction within the stipulated period so that it can be considered in this revision exercise.

With the draft released at both state and district level, the exercise has moved from preparatory updating to public verification. In Cuddalore, Villupuram and Kallakurichi, as elsewhere in Tamil Nadu, the published draft is the document voters should check now, rather than waiting for the final roll in January.
nri_angle: Family members in Tamil Nadu districts can verify their voter entries during the claims window; diaspora readers with relatives in Cuddalore, Villupuram and Kallakurichi can flag the December 11 deadline to them.
author: Diaspora Desk
